# The Tengeri Wastes

ID: `tengeri-wastes` · Refugee camps southwest of Carthara

## Established by the author's latest revision

Wind-carved canyons and jagged cliffs in the Tengeri region southwest of Carthara now shelter Leonin communities driven from their homeland. The Wastes are a region of refugee camps, not a freely chosen ancestral nomadic homeland. Many residents are enslaved or bound to enforced labor, and movement and family visits depend on papers they cannot freely obtain. Bombardment is recurrent, not a single exceptional attack.

The power associated with Lord Numarius dispossessed the Leonin after his people had originally been welcomed as refugees. Other powers repeat false accounts and dehumanizing propaganda. This adopted history revises the earlier setting. It does not establish the original homeland's coordinates, the founding generation, or a complete military chain of command.

## Established in the current prose

[Chapter Three](../../src/content/chapters/03-journeys.ts) follows Hanno into a camp marked “temporary” despite successive shelters becoming homes. The inhabitants maintain classrooms, treatment spaces, work, household records, and personal possessions. Every Leonin carries a flag or emblem of the lost home. Residents disagree over remembrance, education, peace, resistance, and leaving; children and civilians are not an undifferentiated fighting force.

Chuluun keeps one row's records while subject to a labor account himself. Bombardment destroys inhabited facilities and documents families need to trace transferred relatives. A notice then claims an empty militant site and voluntary relocation. Hanno knows those specific claims are false from what he witnessed. He helps his hosts and learns modest practical skills; he neither liberates the camps nor resolves their political choices.
